data.name: Helisia
data.gender_notes: Helisia is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Greek word Ἁλείσα (haleisá), meaning "saving", "healing". Helisia could be derived from the name Helia, which is a short form of Heliane, meaning "shining light". Helisia may also be linked to Helios, the Greek god of the sun. The name Helisia carries the meaning “Saving” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek. Parents who choose Helisia usually hope their child will grow to embody saving and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for a girl who brings hope and healing.
data.etymology: Helisia belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Saving.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Helisia total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_hebrew.name: הליסיה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם הליסיה נגזר מהמילים העבריות 'אל' ו-'ישוע', שפירושן 'אלוהים הוא ישועתי'. השם מבטא את האמונה באלוהים כמושיע ומחסה.

in_greek.name: Ἠλισία
in_greek.meaning: Ἠλισία - ὁ Θεός ἡ σωτηρία μου
in_greek.long_meaning: Ὁ Ἠλισία ὄνομα προέρχεται ἀπὸ τὶς ἑβραϊκὲς λέξεις 'אל' καὶ 'ישוע', ὅπου σημαίνει ὁ Θεὸς ἡ σωτηρία μου. Ἐκφράζει τὴν πίστη εἰς τὸν Θεὸν ὡς Σωτήρα καὶ Προστατευτή.

in_latin.name: Helisia
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Helisia derivatur ex vocibus hebraicis 'אל' et 'ישוע', quae significant 'Deus est salus mea'. Nomen hoc exprimit fidem in Deum ut Salvatorem et Refugium.

in_english.name: Helisia
in_english.long_meaning: The name Helisia originates from Hebrew roots 'אל' (El) and 'ישוע' (Yeshua), meaning 'God is my salvation'. It expresses faith in God as the Savior and Refuge. Historically, the name signifies spiritual protection and divine intervention. In Christian tradition, Helisia symbolizes a deep connection with God's saving grace.

data.cultural_impact: The name Helisia carries a profound impact on the Christian heritage as it embodies the essence of salvation and healing. Helisia's name can serve as a constant reminder of the spiritual renewal and healing that comes from a deep connection to God. It can inspire individuals to transcend their temporal hardships and search for the inner peace and strength that comes from the spiritual realm.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Helisia is a name derived from the Greek word "helios," meaning sun. In Christian symbolism, Helisia represents the light and warmth of God's love shining upon us, guiding us through life's challenges. It is a name for those who seek divine illumination and the strength to rise above adversity.

historical_references.reference: Helisia, daughter of King Heli, was the mother of John the Baptist according to the New Testament. This Helisia is mentioned in the Gospel of Luke (1:5-7). Heli was a priest descended from Aaron (Luke 1:5), and his wife was named Elisheba. Helisia and Heli lived in the town of Gilgal during the reign of King Herod the Great (37-4 BC).
historical_references.context: New Testament, Jewish Priest, Daughter of Heli, Mother of John the Baptist

historical_references.reference: Helisia, also known as Helena of Constantinople, was a Christian saint and the wife of Constantius III, Roman Emperor from 421-425 AD. She is venerated as a saint in the Eastern Orthodox and Roman Catholic Churches. Helisia is particularly remembered for her efforts to recover the True Cross of Jesus Christ. According to legend, she discovered the cross in Jerusalem and returned it to Constantinople in a great procession.
historical_references.context: Christian Saint, Roman Emperor's Wife, Discovery of the True Cross
